structural_findings.title: Exit model is binary — R is {-1.00, +1.618} only
structural_findings.detail: Across all 3265 trades the R-multiple takes only these values: -1R ×2021, +1.618R ×1191, +1R ×53. Every trade is either a clean +1.618R target hit or a -1.00R stop-out (there is no partial exit, no trailing, no scale-out). Consequence: the payoff ratio is structurally fixed at 1.618 for every strategy, so no strategy can be improved by tuning the exit, and **win rate is the only performance lever available**. Any recommendation about 'better risk/reward' is not implementable with the current exit model.
structural_findings.impact: Changes the whole optimisation target: optimise hit rate, not R:R.

structural_findings.title: `min_strength` and `resample_tf` are dead config
structural_findings.detail: `automation/scripts/live_scan.py:206-209` copies `min_strength` and `resample_tf` out of strategy_overrides.json into the per-strategy config, but no code path ever reads them back (the detectors are called with explicit arguments; there is no `**cfg["args"]` spread). Confirmed by grep: the only other references are in param_optimizer.py, which writes them. Consequence: the last three accepted LLM param changes (RSI-Div 2026-10-17, 3-Pushes 2026-10-18, Kell-Cycle 2026-10-20) each applied `resample_tf: 15min` — all three were **no-ops**. Only the `weight` part of those changes had any effect. RSI-Div's own base arg `resample_15m: True` is dead for the same reason.
structural_findings.impact: 3 of the last 3 'optimisations' burned confidence budget on a no-op parameter.

structural_findings.title: `weight` is applied AFTER the confidence gate — it is not a strength filter
structural_findings.detail: live_scan.py order is: LLM grade (1505) → BTC boost (1511) → `conf < min_conf` gate (1517) → grade gate (1520) → **weight scaling (1536)**. The code comment above line 1536 claims weight makes a down-weighted strategy 'fire less often / need more confluence', but by the time the weight is applied the signal has already passed both gates. `weight` therefore only (a) breaks stacking ties on the same ticker+direction (line 747) and (b) scales the confidence published to the AI-Trader (line 1736). It does **not** filter the strategy's own signals.
structural_findings.impact: A weight cut is a weak instrument: it cannot fix a strategy that fires 100% of its trades.

structural_findings.title: The 7d window is statistically thin
structural_findings.detail: 115 trades in 7d across 10 strategies (median 4.5 per strategy), versus 493 in 30d and 3265 all-time. 6 of the 10 strategies have fewer than 8 trades in 7d. Per-strategy 7d numbers are directional, not conclusive; every recommendation in this report is therefore cross-checked against the 30d and all-time windows, and confidence is capped where the windows disagree.
structural_findings.impact: Confidence must be discounted, and per-strategy n<8 findings are labelled anecdotal.

structural_findings.title: Production scientist script reports all-time numbers as '7d'
structural_findings.detail: `automation/scripts/llm_iteration_scientist.py:139-183` filters signals to 7d but applies **no date filter at all to trades**. Its 'PERFORMANCE (7d window)' block therefore reports the full history — 1011 trades for 50-20-Pullback vs 39 in the real 7d window, 701 for CRT vs 33. It also computes `profit_factor` as wins/losses (line 190 — a win/loss *ratio*, not gross profit ÷ gross loss), and it pattern-matches 'B1' such that the B1 agent absorbs all 39 B1-3in1 trades (B1 shows 54 trades instead of 15). Because the 'profit factor' is really a win-rate ratio, **profitable strategies are graded D**: in the manual run of 2026-10-21 09:44 HKT CRT was graded D while showing +27.62R, and 3-Pushes was graded D while showing +34.82R. Seven of ten strategies came out as grade D.
structural_findings.impact: The daily 00:00 HKT run has been grading strategies on wrong data, and its D grades are not evidence that a strategy loses money.

structural_findings.title: The holdout-validated optimiser — the system's best levers — is completely dormant
structural_findings.detail: `automation/config/agent_params.json` holds per-(strategy, ticker) cell configs for 9 strategies, each with `drop_tickers`/`keep_tickers`, `min_conf`, `grade_filter`, `direction`, `weekday_exclude`, `hours` and the exit set (`t2_r`, `breakeven_at_r`, `partial_at_r`, `stop_mult`, `max_bars_held`). These are exactly the levers the 4D analysis needs. But **every entry has `_validated` unset and `validated_on_holdout: false`**, each carrying the note *"not published: did not improve on both the live track and the independent 180-day one-hour track"* (0/9 validated). `live_scan.py:1663` gates the whole block behind `if _ap and _ap.get("_validated")`, so **not one of these levers is applied at runtime**. Matching commit: `1733faa3 feat(optimizer): second independent track — 0 of 9 configurations survive it`.
structural_findings.impact: The system has a correct, holdout-gated optimiser and an LLM loop that pushes mostly-dead parameters. The high-value move is to make the validated path usable, not to keep tuning `weight` — but note SF-9: the *current* configs must not be published as-is. The gate is doing its job; the fix is a better search, not a weaker gate.

structural_findings.title: The +1.618R monoculture is the *pre-override* regime — the new exits are untested
structural_findings.detail: `exit_overrides.json` (written 2026-10-20T14:00:02.325747+00:00, runs=7) carries learned `t2_r` (2.0–3.0) and `breakeven_at_r` (0.5–1.5) for 6 strategies, and `resolve_exit_config` (live_scan.py:902) does read it. But every one of the 1,189 winning trades in the file is exactly +1.618R, because the last trade was recorded at 2026-10-20T13:00Z and the overrides were written at 2026-10-20T14:00Z — **after** the data. Furthermore `rl_arm.assign_arm` only applies an override during that strategy's RL half-period, and 4 strategies (3-Pushes, CRT, B1, B1-3in1) have no override at all and are therefore permanently on the default template.
structural_findings.impact: Do not read the +1.618R monoculture as proof that exits cannot be improved. The first 14-day RL window is the real test, and it has not happened yet.

structural_findings.title: The scientist's LLM parser can never yield a parameter — auto-apply is structurally impossible
structural_findings.detail: `llm_iteration_scientist.py:291` parses the LLM reply with a single regex that demands **pipe-delimited** fields (`GRADE: A|B|C|D | CONFIDENCE: n | DIAGNOSIS: … | REASON: … | SUGGESTED_PARAMS: {…}`). MiniMax-M3 actually answers with **newline-delimited** fields, so the main regex never matches; the partial fallback at lines 306-312 recovers GRADE and CONFIDENCE but leaves `reason` and `suggested_params` empty. `auto_apply` (line 302) requires a non-empty `suggested_params`, so **the scientist can never auto-apply anything**, no matter how confident the model is. Measured on the manual run of 2026-10-21 09:44 HKT (`iteration_scientist_20261021_094417.json`): 10/10 agents have `suggested_params: {}` and `n_auto_applied: 0` — including `yw-two-yang`, which was graded **B with confidence 95** and whose reply explicitly carried `SUGGESTED_PARAMS: {"min_grad…` (truncated out of the diagnosis field). The sibling script `llm_iterate_all.py:91` gets this right — it scrapes `weight` with a loose regex (`r"weight['\"]?\s*[:=]\s*([0-9.]+)"`) that survives any format, which is why `strategy_overrides.json` does contain real applied changes (3 applications, last 2026-10-20) while the scientist's own proposals are always empty. The parser itself was **not** among the changes the remote made on 2026-10-21 (commits `c3ea8421`, `9a05168e`) — those only routed the call through the new shared `automation/src/llm_client.py`, which now returns `(content, error)` and lets the caller see the real cause instead of `KeyError: 'choices'`. But the scientist **discards that error** (`content, _llm_err = chat(...)`, lines 279-281), so a rate-limited call is now reported as *"[Rule-based - LLM unavailable]"* with the HTTP 429 detail thrown away, and `llm_client` itself has **no retry or backoff** for 429. Compounding everything, the script fans out to 10 workers (line 437) against a 5-hour Token Plan window: 8 of 10 calls in the 09:44 run returned HTTP 429 and were replaced by the rule-based fallback, which reuses the broken win/loss-ratio 'profit factor' from SF-5.
structural_findings.impact: The workflow advertises 'Auto-applies high-confidence (>= 60%) parameter changes', but that path has never fired from the scientist. Every 'optimisation' in the audit log came from the other script, and half of those changes were to a dead parameter (SF-2).

structural_findings.title: The optimiser's ticker keep/drop decisions are inverted on the data they were tuned on
structural_findings.detail: `backtest_optimizer.py` reports **0 of 9 configurations survive** on both tracks, and that verdict is correct — but the reason is sharper than 'overfitting'. Replaying each published config on the optimiser's **own holdout** (the last 30% of that strategy's A/B trades, the same split the optimiser used) shows the ticker filter is the problem, and that it points the wrong way: **50-20-Pullback** — base holdout PF 0.942 / -10.5R becomes PF 0.844 / -25.1R once the optimiser's own keep/drop set is applied (-14.6R): drops MES=F which is +10.0R (PF 1.912, n=24) on the very holdout it was tuned on; drops M2K=F which is +4.6R (PF 1.456, n=19) on the very holdout it was tuned on; keeps BTC-USD which is -35.9R (PF 0.767, n=227). **CRT** — base holdout PF 1.019 / +2.4R becomes PF 0.916 / -7.0R once the optimiser's own keep/drop set is applied (-9.4R): drops MNQ=F which is +10.1R (PF 1.533, n=37) on the very holdout it was tuned on; keeps MGC=F which is -5.4R (PF 0.728, n=29); keeps MES=F which is -4.3R (PF 0.839, n=41). **3-Pushes** — base holdout PF 1.179 / +12.5R becomes PF 1.192 / +7.3R once the optimiser's own keep/drop set is applied (-5.2R): drops BTC-USD which is +7.3R (PF 1.428, n=32) on the very holdout it was tuned on. The optimiser never evaluated **B1-3in1** (39 trades, -39.0R, 0.0% win rate) at all: `backtest_optimizer.py` drops every trade whose `direction` is `'none'`, so a strategy that never resolves a direction is invisible to it. The exit-lever search contributes nothing in the live book, because the live exit model is binary (SF-1) — every cell's chosen config is `t2=1.618 be=0.0 pa=0.0`, i.e. the book default. So the only lever that actually moves is the ticker list, and it is being selected on a train sample of 21-379 trades against a per-cell exit-combo search space that can only fit noise.
structural_findings.impact: Do NOT flip the `_validated` gate on these configs — for 50-20-Pullback the published config loses 15R more than doing nothing on the very holdout it was selected for. The gate is currently protecting the book. What is worth doing is the two ticker restrictions that BOTH this report and the optimiser's own holdout data agree on (50-20-Pullback drop BTC-USD, Stair keep MNQ=F only).

structural_findings.title: `agent_weight()` never matches — the optimiser's confidence lever runs on the wrong number
structural_findings.detail: `backtest_optimizer.py:agent_weight()` recovers the RAW confidence of a trade by dividing its published (weight-scaled) confidence by the strategy's weight. It finds that weight by grepping `live_scan.py` with `re.search(r'^\s*"NAME":\s*\{[^}]*"weight":\s*([0-9.]+)', src, re.MULTILINE)` — but `[^}]*` cannot cross the `}` inside the entry's `"args": {...}`, so the pattern never matches and the helper **silently returns 1.0 for every strategy**. Consequence: for 7 of the 9 strategies the reconstructed 'raw confidence' is in fact the *scaled* confidence, and the `min_conf` lever is applied to it — while the live gate (`live_scan.py:1528`, `LLM_MIN_CONF=40` / `LLM_MIN_CONF_BTC=30`) compares the **raw** confidence, because the weight is only applied afterwards (line 1536, SF-3). The optimiser and the live system are therefore calibrating the same lever against two different quantities. The scale error per strategy: **50-20-Pullback** ×0.948, **CRT** ×1.3, **Stair** ×1.1, **3-Pushes** ×1.2, **RSI-Div** ×0.6, **B1** ×0.9, **Kell-Cycle** ×0.7. A `min_conf=65` candidate admits true raw ≥ 50 on CRT but needs raw ≥ 108 on RSI-Div — i.e. the lever looks cheap for up-weighted strategies and impossible for down-weighted ones, which is exactly backwards for a confidence floor.
structural_findings.impact: One published cell uses `min_conf` (Two-Yang BTC-USD, min_conf=65, weight 0.8), so there is no live impact today — but that cell would behave differently live than in the simulation if the `_validated` gate were ever passed. The search itself was distorted for every strategy, so the min_conf variants it explored were not the ones it should have.

structural_findings.title: The 'second, independent track' is independent in resolution, not in time
structural_findings.detail: `btopt_2026-10-20.md` states the two tracks *"share no trades and cover different periods"*. The second track spans 182 days (2026-04-20 → 2026-10-20), but its **holdout** — the last 30% of its trades — lands in the SAME recent window as the live track's holdout, because the split is per-strategy and chronological: **H-Pattern** — live holdout 2026-09-21→2026-10-19 overlaps the second track's holdout 2026-08-27→2026-10-19 by 27 days (100% of the live holdout window) **Kell-Cycle** — live holdout 2026-09-10→2026-10-19 overlaps the second track's holdout 2026-08-26→2026-10-20 by 39 days (100% of the live holdout window) **Stair** — live holdout 2026-09-14→2026-10-20 overlaps the second track's holdout 2026-09-01→2026-10-20 by 36 days (100% of the live holdout window). The part of the second track that IS genuinely earlier in time (its training window) is largely unusable: `load_bars()` fetches only 60 days of 5-minute bars, so only 33-37% of each strategy's second-track trades have bars to replay against; `prepare_trade()` returns None for the rest and they are dropped without a word. The verdict itself survives this — the holdout is 100% inside the window — but the *independence* it claims does not: the second track tests robustness to bar resolution and to the trade population, not to the market regime, at exactly the point where the verdict is made.
structural_findings.impact: '0 of 9 survive' is a weaker statement than the report implies. A config that fails the second track may be fitted to the recent regime rather than overfitted to the sample. That argues for keeping the `_validated` gate closed (SF-9) and for extending the bars window before treating the second track as out-of-time evidence.
